integrity: The proof uses the published minimal bisubset inequality description, computes the intrinsic projected normal of every facet, proves a global upper bound and uniqueness from the coordinate facets, and proves by an exact two-parameter reduction that every other facet is farther away. The exceptional rank-two incenter segment is derived directly from all six facet distances. Finite computation is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the standard Ardila--Escobar harmonic-polytope realization and the inherited Euclidean metric. It does not compute the circumradius, John ellipsoid, or affine-invariant metric data. A residual originality risk remains for an equivalent generic Chebyshev-center result on the same H-description under different terminology.
title: Exact Euclidean inradius and incenter transition of the harmonic polytope
